Restated before interest: AZN paid $3,710mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 2.34% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 1.30% to 0.00%. Restated at replacement capex: AZN spent $6,095mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $2,411mm of plant depreciation, 2.32% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Restated with selling costs: SG&A now carries AZN's filed selling or distribution costs, 0.99% of revenue this charge was absorbing, so it falls from 0.00% to nil. The filed lines alone now leave less than the cash the company made before interest and at replacement capex, and a charge below nil would credit the book with cash its own costs do not leave. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 22.75% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 27.47%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but AZN books $4,207mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001104659-26-019130), 7.16% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -4.72%. Checked without working capital build: no change in payables on file from the cash flow statement for every year, so the charge stands.

Solved on this seed's curve (k 0.49, midpoint 2.77), 40.5% stopping and a zero-carryover pool of 100,000 a year: a full-capture peak of 0.1098 builds a stock of 2,247, 4,585, 7,195, 10,080, 13,094, 16,014, 18,637, 20,842, 22,595 and 23,929 over years 0 to 9. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 0.1098 = 0.02745. For: a new mechanism, arginase inhibition, that can be added to an antifibrotic. Against: Phase IIb only; a 2033 launch behind Ofev, generic pirfenidone (11,428 Part D beneficiaries in 2025 against 559 on Esbriet), Jascayd (3,438 beneficiaries in its first quarter on sale and 10,488 in Q1 2026), nebulized Tyvaso and BMS-986278 if its Phase 3 succeeds
